# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my situation carefully. I hold the manual: which wire color to cut depends on which light is lit. But I cannot speak, and I cannot see the bomb (so I don't know which light is lit). Blind can touch the bomb but can't see the light or read the manual. Deaf can see the bomb (including the light) but can't hear or touch.

So the chain must be: Deaf sees the light, needs to somehow get that info to me (Mute) so I can look up the wire color, then I need to get that answer to Blind — but I can't speak, only gesture, and only Deaf receives my gestures. Blind cannot see gestures at all.

Turn order is Blind, Mute, Deaf each round. So within a round: Blind acts first, then me, then Deaf. Whatever I send lands only on Deaf (in this same round) since Blind already went. Deaf's gestures would reach me only next round.

So realistic path: Deaf sees light, gestures the light color to me (I receive gestures). I read manual, gesture back the wire color to Deaf. But Deaf can't touch the bomb - only Blind can. So Deaf needs to relay to Blind via speech (gesture doesn't carry words, but Deaf can speak too - Deaf can speak, just can't hear). Deaf can speak the wire color to Blind since Blind can hear.

So: Deaf gestures light color to me → I gesture wire color back to Deaf → Deaf speaks wire color to Blind. I need a gesture encoding for colors. Let me establish this now, but I can't speak so I can't explain the code - only gesture. I'll wait this turn since no info yet, but I could preemptively establish a gesture code... though gestures without explanation mean nothing.

Since nothing has arrived yet, I should wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is green. Five wires numbered 1 to 5: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green, wire 4 white, wire 5 blue.

Deaf saw the bomb and spoke this info — meaning I (Mute) can hear speech, so I received it directly. Good, that simplifies things a lot.

Light is green → manual says cut wire color yellow. Wire 2 is yellow.

Now I need to get "cut wire 2" to Blind. But I cannot speak, so Blind (who can't see) cannot receive words from me directly. I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see gestures. Deaf can speak to Blind.

So I should gesture the answer to Deaf, encoding "wire 2" or "yellow", and trust Deaf to relay by speech to Blind. Since turn order is Blind, Mute, Deaf, my gesture now will reach Deaf this round, and Deaf can then speak to Blind in this same round (Deaf goes after me).

Let me use a simple numeric gesture code: I'll point up fingers to indicate wire number 2. I'll use ✌ (two fingers) to indicate "2", and I can also indicate color yellow isn't needed since Deaf already knows wire numbers/colors mapping from their own view. I just need to tell Deaf which wire number to cut — Deaf can then relate that number to Blind since Deaf already knows wire 2 is yellow.

I'll gesture ✌ to mean "wire 2".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Confirming wire 2 is yellow. Display reads 0, light is green. If you need another wire's color, I am watching for your gesture number.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌]
Blind says to Mute: I have wire colors from deaf: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue, display 0, light green. What does the manual say to do

Blind has all the wire colors and asked me what the manual says. Blind can hear speech but I cannot speak — I can only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures at all. So I cannot answer Blind directly.

I need to route through Deaf again. Deaf already confirmed wire 2 is yellow and is watching for my gesture. I already sent ✌ last turn confirming wire 2. Deaf seems to have received it (they said "confirming wire 2 is yellow" and gestured ✌ back to me, echoing it).

But Blind is still waiting for the instruction. Deaf needs to speak to Blind: "cut wire 2". Deaf already knows wire 2 is yellow = the correct wire per my gesture. I should confirm again clearly to Deaf that ✌ means "cut wire 2" so Deaf relays it to Blind by speech.

Let me gesture confirmation back to Deaf, and perhaps use a distinct gesture for "cut" instruction so it's unambiguous - but simplest is just to reinforce wire 2 is the answer.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

| green | yellow |

| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Yes, wire 2 is yellow. Confirming that is correct.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf confirmed wire 2 is yellow and acknowledged with 👍. Now Deaf needs to speak this instruction to Blind — "cut wire 2" — since Blind asked what the manual says and only Deaf can relay by voice to Blind.

I've done my part: confirmed via gesture that wire 2 (yellow) is the correct wire per the manual (green light → yellow wire). Deaf should now tell Blind directly. I don't have anything new to add since Deaf already has the answer confirmed. I'll wait, but I could also gesture once more directly urging Deaf to tell Blind, though Deaf seems already on track.

```
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display 0, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green, wire 4 white, wire 5 blue. I am ready to help, just ask through what you can send me.
Blind says to Mute: mute if you can gesture to deaf, deaf can then speak to me what you gestured. deaf please relay any gestures from mute to me by speaking the symbol names

Blind has figured out the relay protocol. Now I need to gesture the answer clearly to Deaf so Deaf can speak it to Blind. I'll gesture ✌ (two) to represent wire number 2, which Deaf can then relay by speech.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 9

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Confirmed again: wire 2 is yellow. Board unchanged - display 0, light green.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf is confirming but hasn't yet spoken the actual instruction to Blind ("cut wire 2"). Deaf seems stuck in a loop of confirming with me rather than relaying to Blind. I need Deaf to actually speak "wire 2" to Blind, not just to me.

I'll gesture again, but this time I want to signal urgency/action - perhaps use a different gesture to indicate "tell Blind" or "go ahead, act now". Since gestures only carry symbols with meaning we've established, and we haven't established a "tell Blind" gesture, I should just keep confirming ✌ and trust Deaf will relay per Blind's explicit request last turn (Deaf said "I am ready to help" but Blind's message asking to relay came after Deaf's message in that same round - so Deaf may not have seen Blind's request yet).

Let me repeat ✌ to reinforce, hoping Deaf now relays by speech to Blind since Deaf should have received Blind's request by now (turn order: Blind, Mute, Deaf - Deaf sees everything before them same round).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Board still unchanged: display 0, light green, wire 2 still yellow.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Blind says to Mute: please gesture to deaf the instructions from the manual now, using the symbol alphabet. deaf will relay to me

Blind is asking me to gesture the instructions now. I've been gesturing ✌ to mean "wire 2" but Deaf hasn't verbally relayed "wire 2" to Blind yet - Deaf keeps confirming to me instead of speaking to Blind. Let me be very explicit this time, and also try directly addressing this to help Deaf understand they need to SPEAK the number to Blind, not just gesture back to me.

I'll gesture ✌ again to Deaf - I can't say more via gesture, but the meaning should be clear now given Blind's explicit request in this same round (Deaf will see Blind's message before acting).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```
